html:
SMTO-TSK-0033 — That workflow can't be found or saved

GUID: 3297fad5-56ff-4f5e-930f-b9342e553491
Slug: recipe-unavailable
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • The workflow you picked no longer exists, perhaps because it was deleted, or the message you picked can't be saved as a workflow.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the page and open Workflows to see which workflows still exist. The one you selected may have been deleted in another window or by someone else.
  2. If it is gone, select New workflow, or choose Save to workflow beside the message you want to repeat. A fresh workflow takes the place of the missing one.
  3. If saving a message failed, choose a different finished message from the conversation. Some messages can't be turned into a workflow.

What success looks like

  • The workflow appears in Workflows and opens, previews or runs without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't create several copies of the same workflow trying to get past this; check Workflows first.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The requested workflow (recipe) record is missing or archived, or the selected run is not capturable and the capture candidate returned no valid workflow.

What this means

  • A selected recipe record is absent, capture says not saveable or the capture response lacks a valid recipe object. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • A selected recipe record is absent, capture says not saveable or the capture response lacks a valid recipe object.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish missing recipe identity from source-run capture ineligibility using the actual candidate reason.

How to fix it

  • Re-list workflows (GET /api/agent/recipes) and use a current recipe_id; for capture, use a completed request whose candidate reports saveable. Earlier run history stays as history; a workflow run must produce its own new results rather than reuse old ones.
  • Select an available recipe or a supported completed run for capture. Keep previous operation receipts as history; a recipe must establish fresh execution evidence.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • An available recipe or supported saveable candidate passes ordinary admission.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
